# wal-store

Key value store that appends every mutation to a write-ahead log first, so a process killed between writes and checkpoints recovers exactly the committed state.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m wal_store --path ./store recover
    python3 -m wal_store --path ./store put <key> --value-file <path>
    python3 -m wal_store --path ./store get <key>

## Public interface

`wal_store.Store(path)` opens the store directory. The directory must
exist; opening a missing path raises `FileNotFoundError` (the `put` command
line subcommand creates it).
- `put(key, value) -> None` records a mutation.
- `get(key) -> bytes | None` reads the current value.
- `delete(key) -> None` records a removal.
- `commit() -> int` advances the durable sequence number.
- `recover() -> dict` replays the log and reports what it applied.
- `compact() -> dict` rewrites committed history into one tight log and
  reclaims the old space, without changing the committed state or the
  durable sequence.
- `scan(start=None, end=None) -> ScanCursor` opens an ordered read-only
  cursor over the committed snapshot pinned at that moment.
- `stats() -> dict` reports sequence, entries and bytes.

## Scanning

`scan()` works on both open forms and never touches the write path. The
returned cursor is an iterator of `(key, value)` pairs in bytewise key
order — keys compare by their raw UTF-8 bytes and values come back as the
exact stored bytes, with no encoding conversion — covering `start`
inclusive through `end` exclusive; a `None` endpoint leaves that side
unbounded, so `scan()` walks everything. Keys that only ever appeared in
delete records never show up, a key overwritten any number of times yields
only its last committed value, and empty values scan like any other. A
writer's uncommitted changes are not part of the snapshot; a read-only
store scans the snapshot it pinned at open.

The snapshot is materialised once when the cursor opens, so later commits,
compaction, crash recovery and reclamation of the old log space never
change what the cursor yields, and the same snapshot scans to the identical
sequence before and after compaction. Scanning never replays the log,
takes no lock and keeps no history in memory, so its cost is independent
of the log's length. A `start` that sorts after `end` raises `ValueError`,
as does reading from a cursor after `close()` (the cursor is also a
context manager).

`wal_store.Store(path, read_only=True)` opens an isolated reader. Any
number of read-only processes may coexist with the single writer in the
same directory. A reader takes no lock and never creates or changes a
file; it pins a snapshot at open time and every `get` reads from that one
complete committed snapshot, so uncommitted mutations, a half-written
commit, a torn record or a half-finished shrink are never visible.
Successive reads from the same reader may advance across snapshots only by
reopening; each read is of one fully committed snapshot. Reads do not
replay the log and do not block the writer: killing or suspending a reader
never affects the writer's commits, recovery or stats. `put`, `delete`,
`commit` and `recover` are rejected on a read-only store; `stats` reports
the pinned snapshot and `get` is the normal way to read it. Readers serve
from the atomically replaced `wal.ckp` sidecar (and the committed log
prefix), so directories written by older versions open directly.

`wal_store.inject_tear(source, destination, offset)` is a verification aid:
it writes a byte-for-byte copy of `source` cut at exactly `offset` bytes (a
replica of a process killed at that write position) to `destination` and
leaves the source untouched. Either argument may be a store directory, in
which case its `wal.log` is used. A negative or past-the-end offset raises
`IndexError`. It is never used by the normal write path.

## Recovery

`recover()` returns a report with three integer fields, in this key order:

- `applied` — committed put/delete records replayed into the state,
- `discarded` — torn tail records dropped (at most one, the unfinished final
  write left by a process killed mid append; `0` on a clean log),
- `seq` — the durable sequence number after recovery.

A record killed halfway through is not a mutation: it is discarded and the
recovered state is exactly the last committed state. An empty log recovers
to an empty state, which is a normal result. Recovery truncates the dirty
tail and the next commit uses `seq + 1`, no matter how often the store is
reopened.

### Recovery may itself be killed

Recovery is an idempotent, kill-safe convergence. Interrupting it at any
point — while the dirty tail is being dropped or the log is being rebuilt —
and reopening any number of times reaches exactly the state and the report
of one clean recovery, with exit code `0`; the durable sequence never
regresses and the next commit is always `seq + 1`.

Two internal sidecar files in the store directory make this work; they are
not part of the public API and are maintained entirely below the write
path:

- `wal.ckp` is an atomically replaced copy of the log prefix ending at the
  most recent commit marker. A log torn at *any* offset — even offset 0, or
  inside the committed prefix — is silently rebuilt from it, so a
  half-finished convergence can never be mistaken for a torn tail or for
  corruption.
- `wal.rec` is a small marker written after validation and before the
  repair, recording the clean prefix length and the discarded count. A
  repair interrupted mid-copy is simply repeated on reopen, and the marker
  keeps `discarded` stable across reopens and repeated recoveries until the
  next successful commit closes the epoch.

Only the final record may be incomplete. Any incomplete record elsewhere,
a length out of bounds, unparseable content, or a duplicate/regressing
sequence is corruption: recovery raises `wal_store.CorruptLogError`
(a subclass of `ValueError`) and stops without applying or removing
anything.

The command line `recover` prints the report as one compact JSON line with
the same key order and a trailing newline, e.g.
`{"applied":2,"discarded":0,"seq":1}`. Discarding a torn tail is not an
error and the exit code is `0`; corruption prints one explanatory line to
standard error and exits `3` without printing the JSON line.

## Compaction

`compact()` reclaims history without sacrificing any committed state. When
it finishes, the log contains exactly the live committed key/values: one
put frame per currently committed key, in sorted key order, followed by a
base commit marker that carries the pre-compaction sequence. Deleted keys
are gone for good — a deleted key can never reappear — and overwritten keys
keep only their final value. The durable sequence number is unchanged, so
the next `commit()` writes `seq + 1` and subsequent commits continue the
strict sequence as if no rewrite had happened. The empty committed state
(including "everything was deleted") compacts to an empty log.

`compact()` returns the same three-field report shape as `recover()`:
`applied` is the number of live puts the new log contains, `discarded` is
always `0` and `seq` is the preserved sequence. Uncommitted session changes
make it raise `ValueError`; commit or discard them first.

Compaction is a kill-safe, idempotent convergence like recovery. The new
image is assembled in memory and durably staged as the `wal.cmp` sidecar
(an atomically replaced complete file, never an in-place edit), then
published in two atomic steps — `wal.ckp` first and `wal.log` second —
before the staging file is removed. A process killed at any point, any
number of times, leaves a store that finishes the identical publish on the
next open: the recovered state is exactly the last committed state, the
sequence never regresses and the resulting log/sidecar bytes are
byte-identical to one uninterrupted compaction. Repeating compaction on an
already compact store produces the same bytes.

Live read-only stores are unaffected: they keep serving the complete
snapshot they pinned before, during and after compaction (it lands on the
other half of the same log-versus-checkpoint pair readers already choose
between), while fresh readers open the compacted snapshot. No reader ever
sees a mix of old and new bytes, a half-written file, or content whose
space was reclaimed; killing a reader does not disturb compaction and
killing the compactor does not disturb a reader. Compaction introduces no
new limits beyond the existing single-writer rule, and directories written
by older versions compact directly with no conversion step.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

One writer at a time; no cross-process locking.
Values are bytes; encoding is the caller concern.
No replication; compaction is a writer-initiated rewrite, not background
garbage collection.

1	"""Write-ahead log key value store.
2	
3	Every mutation is first appended to a framed log. A commit marker is the
4	only thing that advances the durable sequence number. When a store is opened,
5	any tail that was never committed (including a record torn by a hard kill) is
6	discarded, so recovery always yields exactly the committed state.
7	
8	Only the very last log record may be incomplete: a process killed while
9	appending leaves at most one torn record, which is dropped without being
10	applied. Any other framing failure -- a truncated record in the middle, a
11	length field out of bounds, unparseable content, or a duplicate/regressing
12	commit sequence -- is corruption, and recovery raises ``CorruptLogError``
13	without touching the store.
14	
15	Recovery itself may be killed at any point, any number of times. Two small
16	sidecar files in the store directory, both maintained below the write path,
17	make the convergence protocol kill-safe and its report stable:
18	
19	``wal.ckp``
20	    A byte-for-byte copy of the log prefix ending at the most recent commit
21	    marker, replaced atomically (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync)
22	    only after that commit frame is durable. A log torn at *any* offset --
23	    even offset 0, or inside the committed prefix -- is rebuilt from it, so
24	    the durable sequence number never regresses. It is also the published
25	    snapshot read-only processes pin (see below).
26	
27	``wal.rec``
28	    A recovery marker written only after a log needing repair has passed
29	    full validation and only *before* the atomic rebuild starts. It records
30	    the clean prefix length and whether a torn record was discarded. Its
31	    presence makes a rebuild interrupted mid-copy converge on reopen (the
32	    rebuild is simply repeated) and keeps the reported ``discarded`` count
33	    stable across reopens and repeated recoveries. It is removed by the next
34	    successful commit.
35	
36	Range scans (``Store.scan(start, end)``) open an ordered read-only cursor
37	over the complete committed snapshot pinned at the moment the cursor is
38	opened. The cursor yields ``(key, value)`` pairs in bytewise key order --
39	keys compare by their raw UTF-8 bytes, with no encoding conversion -- from
40	``start`` (inclusive) to ``end`` (exclusive); a ``None`` endpoint leaves
41	that side unbounded. Keys that only ever appear in delete records never
42	show up, a key overwritten many times yields only its last committed value,
43	and empty values scan like any other. The snapshot is materialised once
44	when the cursor opens, so commits, compaction or crash recovery during the
45	scan never change it, reclaiming the old log space cannot break it, and the
46	cost of a scan is independent of how long the log's history is. A reversed
47	range (``start`` after ``end``) and any read from a closed cursor raise
48	``ValueError``.
49	
50	Read-only processes (``Store(path, read_only=True)``) take no lock and never
51	create or modify a file. At open each one picks the highest committed prefix
52	available at that instant -- the validated ``wal.log`` prefix or ``wal.ckp``
53	-- scans it once into memory and serves every ``get`` from that index.
54	Because the chosen image is complete and is only ever replaced atomically
55	(never edited in place), a refresh caught mid-rename, a half-written commit,
56	a torn record, or a log being rebuilt, shrunk or compacted can never expose
57	partial bytes: each read lands on one full committed snapshot that was
58	current at or after the open. A directory written by an older version is
59	opened the same way from its log and checkpoint. Reads never replay the log
60	afterwards, so their cost is independent of history and they never block
61	the writer; a reader that is killed or simply hangs changes nothing on disk.
62	
63	Compaction (``Store.compact()``) rewrites the committed history into one
64	tight image without losing a byte of committed state. The compacted log
65	holds exactly the live puts -- one per currently committed key, in sorted
66	key order -- followed by a *base commit* marker carrying the pre-compaction
67	sequence number. The durable sequence keeps that value, so the next commit
68	is ``seq + 1`` and every later commit continues the strict sequence; keys
69	that were deleted never come back. The image is assembled in memory and
70	staged as the atomically replaced ``wal.cmp`` sidecar; finishing installs
71	it as ``wal.ckp`` first and as ``wal.log`` second. Every intermediate state
72	is therefore either the pair of old files or the pair of complete new
73	images, which is precisely the two-image world the reader already chooses
74	between: a kill anywhere leaves a state reopening converges by simply
75	repeating the finish, and interrupting compaction any number of times
76	produces the same bytes as one clean run. Live readers keep serving their
77	pinned old snapshots (the inode survives on Unix; on Windows readers hold
78	no writer-side fd) and new readers land on the new snapshot, never a mix,
79	a half-written file or a byte that was already reclaimed.
80	
81	The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log boundary,
82	the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can never move
83	backwards. Every repair step is either idempotent or an atomic rename; a
84	kill between any two steps leaves a state the next open converges from to
85	the identical result.
86	
87	Log frame layout (all integers big-endian)::
88	
89	    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+
90	    | b"WAL2" | payload_length | header_crc | payload              | crc32   |
91	    | 4 bytes | 8 bytes        | 4 bytes    | metadata\\n<value>    | 4 bytes |
92	    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+
93	
94	``header_crc`` is the crc32 of the magic and length bytes. It makes a
95	partial header that borrows bytes from a following frame fail validation,
96	so an incomplete record in the middle of the log reads as corruption while
97	a genuinely short final header reads as a torn tail.
98	
99	Metadata is a compact JSON object: ``{"t":"p","k":key}`` for puts,
100	``{"t":"d","k":key}`` for deletes, ``{"t":"c","s":seq}`` for ordinary
101	commits and ``{"t":"b","s":seq}`` for the base commit that closes a
102	compacted log. The two carry the sequence identically; a base marker is
103	additionally required to be the first commit marker in its file.
104	The raw value bytes follow the first newline, so values need no encoding.
105	"""

118	class CorruptLogError(ValueError):
119	    """The write-ahead log is corrupt, not merely missing a torn tail.
120	
121	    A single incomplete final record is a normal crash remnant and is
122	    discarded during recovery. Anything else that fails framing, checksum,
123	    metadata or commit-sequence validation is corruption; recovery stops
124	    without applying or removing anything.
125	    """

128	class ScanCursor:
129	    """Ordered read-only cursor over one pinned committed snapshot.
130	
131	    Created by :meth:`Store.scan`. Iterating yields ``(key, value)`` pairs
132	    in bytewise key order -- keys ordered by their raw UTF-8 bytes, values
133	    returned as the exact stored bytes -- covering the range given at open:
134	    the start key inclusive, the end key exclusive, either side unbounded
135	    when its endpoint was ``None``.
136	
137	    The snapshot is fully materialised when the cursor opens, so later
138	    commits, compaction, crash recovery or reclamation of the old log space
139	    never change what the cursor yields, and closing the store it came from
140	    does not disturb it. The cursor is an iterator; it is also a context
141	    manager, and ``close()`` releases the snapshot early. Reading from a
142	    closed cursor raises ``ValueError``.
143	    """
144	
145	    def __init__(self, items):
146	        # ``items`` is the materialised snapshot: (key, value) pairs already
147	        # sorted by the keys' raw UTF-8 bytes and clipped to the range.
148	        self._items = items
149	        self._pos = 0
150	        self._closed = False
151	
152	    def __iter__(self) -> "ScanCursor":
153	        return self
154	
155	    def __next__(self):
156	        if self._closed:
157	            raise ValueError("scan cursor is closed")
158	        if self._pos >= len(self._items):
159	            raise StopIteration
160	        item = self._items[self._pos]
161	        self._pos += 1
162	        return item
163	
164	    @property
165	    def closed(self) -> bool:
166	        return self._closed
167	
168	    def close(self) -> None:
169	        self._items = []
170	        self._closed = True
171	
172	    def __enter__(self) -> "ScanCursor":
173	        return self
174	
175	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
176	        self.close()

179	LOG_NAME = "wal.log"
180	_CHECKPOINT_NAME = "wal.ckp"
181	_MARKER_NAME = "wal.rec"
182	_COMPACT_NAME = "wal.cmp"
183	
184	_MAGIC = b"WAL2"
185	_PREFIX = 12  # 4 bytes magic + 8 bytes payload length
186	_HEADER = 16   # prefix + 4 bytes crc32 of the prefix
187	_TRAILER = 4   # crc32 of the payload
188	_MAX_PAYLOAD = 1 << 40
189	
190	_OP_PUT = "p"
191	_OP_DELETE = "d"
192	_OP_COMMIT = "c"
193	_OP_BASE = "b"
194	_COMMIT_OPS = (_OP_COMMIT, _OP_BASE)

196	# os.open defaults to the C runtime's text mode on Windows, which would
197	# expand every "\n" to "\r\n" inside os.write and inflate the log on disk.
198	# Forcing binary keeps the log bytes identical on every platform; the flag
199	# does not exist elsewhere, where it is 0.
200	_O_BINARY = getattr(os, "O_BINARY", 0)

203	def _encode_frame(op: str, value: bytes = b"", key: str | None = None,
204	                  seq: int | None = None) -> bytes:
205	    meta: dict[str, object] = {"t": op}
206	    if key is not None:
207	        meta["k"] = key
208	    if seq is not None:
209	        meta["s"] = seq
210	    head = json.dumps(meta, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
211	    payload = head + b"\n" + value
212	    prefix = _MAGIC + len(payload).to_bytes(8, "big")
213	    header = prefix + zlib.crc32(prefix).to_bytes(4, "big")
214	    return header + payload + zlib.crc32(payload).to_bytes(4, "big")
215

217	def _iter_frames(f):
218	    """Scan an open binary log file from position 0.
219	
220	    For every intact frame yields
221	    ``("frame", meta, value, start, end)``. Scanning stops with either no
222	    terminal event (clean EOF), ``("torn", start)`` for a single incomplete
223	    final frame, or ``("invalid", start)`` for a frame that fails framing,
224	    header/payload checksum or metadata parsing. With the header checksum a
225	    partial header that borrows bytes from a following record cannot survive,
226	    so a short read landing exactly at EOF is reliably the one unfinished
227	    record a single writer was appending when it died; bytes left beyond such
228	    a read instead make it corruption.
229	    """
230	    f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
231	    eof = f.tell()
232	    f.seek(0)
233	    while True:
234	        start = f.tell()
235	        header = f.read(_HEADER)
236	        if not header:
237	            return
238	        if len(header) < _HEADER:
239	            # Trailing bytes of a frame header are a torn tail only when
240	            # nothing follows them; a gap anywhere else is corruption.
241	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
242	                   else ("invalid", start))
243	            return
244	        if header[:4] != _MAGIC:
245	            yield "invalid", start
246	            return
247	        if int.from_bytes(header[_PREFIX:], "big") != zlib.crc32(
248	                header[:_PREFIX]):
249	            yield "invalid", start
250	            return
251	        length = int.from_bytes(header[4:_PREFIX], "big")
252	        if length > _MAX_PAYLOAD:
253	            yield "invalid", start
254	            return
255	        payload = f.read(length)
256	        checksum = f.read(_TRAILER)
257	        if len(payload) < length or len(checksum) < _TRAILER:
258	            # Only the single final record may be incomplete.
259	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
260	                   else ("invalid", start))
261	            return
262	        if int.from_bytes(checksum, "big") != zlib.crc32(payload):
263	            yield "invalid", start
264	            return
265	        newline = payload.find(b"\n")
266	        if newline < 0:
267	            yield "invalid", start
268	            return
269	        try:
270	            meta = json.loads(payload[:newline])
271	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
272	            yield "invalid", start
273	            return
274	        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not isinstance(meta.get("t"), str):
275	            yield "invalid", start
276	            return
277	        yield "frame", meta, payload[newline + 1:], start, f.tell()
278

280	def _fsync_dir(path: str) -> None:
281	    """Fsync a directory so a nearby rename/unlink is durable.
282	
283	    Windows cannot open directories for fsync and raises ``PermissionError``
284	    (access denied); directory entries there are made durable by the file's
285	    own flush-on-rename, so skipping the directory fsync keeps store creation
286	    working everywhere. Other platforms occasionally refuse the directory
287	    open or the fsync the same way (restrictive mounts, virtualised FSes);
288	    that is likewise best-effort -- the file's own fsync is what carries the
289	    data -- so a ``PermissionError`` at either step never aborts store
290	    creation or a commit/compaction.
291	    """
292	    if sys.platform == "win32":
293	        return
294	    try:
295	        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
296	    except PermissionError:
297	        return
298	    try:
299	        try:
300	            os.fsync(fd)
301	        except PermissionError:
302	            # Some non-Windows mounts reject directory fsync the same way.
303	            pass
304	    finally:
305	        os.close(fd)

314	def inject_tear(source, destination, offset):
315	    """Copy a log cut at exactly ``offset`` bytes, for bytewise verification.
316	
317	    Produces ``destination`` containing the first ``offset`` bytes of
318	    ``source`` -- a replica of a process killed precisely when the write had
319	    reached that byte offset. The source file is never modified. Either path
320	    argument may be a store directory, in which case its ``wal.log`` is used.
321	
322	    ``offset`` must satisfy ``0 <= offset <= len(source)``; a negative or
323	    past-the-end offset raises ``IndexError``. The full-length copy
324	    (``offset == len(source)``) is the clean control case.
325	
326	    Verification aid only; the normal write path never calls this.
327	    """
328	    if not isinstance(offset, int) or isinstance(offset, bool):
329	        raise TypeError("offset must be an integer byte offset")
330	
331	    src = os.path.join(source, LOG_NAME) if os.path.isdir(source) else source
332	    dst = (os.path.join(destination, LOG_NAME)
333	           if os.path.isdir(destination) else destination)
334	
335	    size = os.path.getsize(src)
336	    if offset < 0 or offset > size:
337	        raise IndexError(
338	            f"tear offset {offset} out of range for log of {size} bytes")
339	    if os.path.abspath(src) == os.path.abspath(dst):
340	        raise ValueError("tear destination must differ from the source log")
341	
342	    remaining = offset
343	    with open(src, "rb") as fsrc, open(dst, "wb") as fdst:
344	        while remaining:
345	            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
346	            if not chunk:  # pragma: no cover - size came from the same file
347	                raise IndexError("source log shrank while copying")
348	            fdst.write(chunk)
349	            remaining -= len(chunk)
350	        fdst.truncate(offset)
351	        os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
352	    return dst

355	class Store:
356	    """A single-writer key value store backed by an append-only log.
357	
358	    ``path`` must be an existing store directory; the log file inside it is
359	    created on first use. Opening a missing directory raises
360	    ``FileNotFoundError`` and opening a path that is not a directory raises
361	    ``OSError``.
362	
363	    With ``read_only=True`` the store is opened purely for reading. No file
364	    is ever created or modified, and no lock is taken: any number of
365	    read-only processes may coexist with the one writer. The reader pins the
366	    committed snapshot current at open time -- the highest committed prefix
367	    of ``wal.log`` or of the atomically replaced ``wal.ckp`` sidecar --
368	    scans it once, and serves every ``get`` from that in-memory index. The
369	    snapshot is independent of the log's later history, so a read never
370	    replays the log and cannot block the writer, and uncommitted bytes, a
371	    half-written commit, a torn record or a half-finished rebuild are never
372	    visible. ``put``, ``delete``, ``commit``, ``recover`` and ``compact``
373	    are rejected on a read-only store; ``stats`` reports the pinned
374	    snapshot.
375	
376	    ``scan(start, end)`` -- on either open form -- returns a
377	    :class:`ScanCursor` over the complete committed snapshot pinned at the
378	    moment of the call, yielding ``(key, value)`` pairs in bytewise key
379	    order from ``start`` (inclusive) to ``end`` (exclusive); a ``None``
380	    endpoint leaves that side unbounded. Uncommitted session changes of a
381	    writer are not part of the snapshot. The cursor reads from memory only:
382	    it never touches the log, takes no lock, and is unaffected by later
383	    commits, compaction, recovery or the store closing.
384	    """
385	
386	    def __init__(self, path: str, read_only: bool = False):
387	        self._dir = path
388	        self._path = os.path.join(path, LOG_NAME)
389	        self._ckp_path = os.path.join(path, _CHECKPOINT_NAME)
390	        self._marker_path = os.path.join(path, _MARKER_NAME)
391	        self._cmp_path = os.path.join(path, _COMPACT_NAME)
392	        self._read_only = read_only
393	
394	        # Recovery needs a directory to replay; a missing target is an error
395	        # at open time, not an implicit create.
396	        if not os.path.exists(path):
397	            raise FileNotFoundError(
398	                f"store directory does not exist: {path!r}")
399	        if not os.path.isdir(path):
400	            raise OSError(f"store path is not a directory: {path!r}")
401	
402	        self._data: dict[str, bytes] = {}
403	        self._seq = 0
404	        self._entries = 0
405	        self._pending = 0
406	        self._closed = False
407	        self._corrupt = False
408	        # Committed value of each key this session has touched since the
409	        # last commit (None when the key was absent); lets a scan pin the
410	        # committed snapshot without replaying the log.
411	        self._touched: dict[str, bytes | None] = {}
412	        # Torn records dropped in this recovery epoch; wal.rec carries it
413	        # across processes until the next commit.
414	        self._discarded = 0
415	
416	        if read_only:
417	            # A read-only open holds no writable fd and never takes a lock;
418	            # leave the writer fd slot unset for clarity.
419	            self._fd = -1
420	            self._open_read_only()
421	            return
422	
423	        log_created = not os.path.exists(self._path)
424	        self._fd = os.open(self._path,
425	                           os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | _O_BINARY,
426	                           0o644)
427	        if log_created:
428	            os.fsync(self._fd)
429	            _fsync_dir(path)
430	
431	        self._converge_on_open()
432	
433	    # -- log scanning and validation --------------------------------------
434	
435	    def _read_log(self, path=None):
436	        frames = []
437	        terminal = None
438	        with open(path or self._path, "rb") as f:
439	            for event in _iter_frames(f):
440	                if event[0] == "frame":
441	                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
442	                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
443	                else:
444	                    terminal = event
445	        return frames, terminal
446	
447	    @staticmethod
448	    def _validate(frames, terminal):
449	        """Validate every frame and the strictly increasing commit sequence.
450	
451	        Returns ``(committed_end, last_seq)`` -- the byte offset just past
452	        the last commit marker and its sequence number. An ``"invalid"``
453	        terminal is corruption and raises ``CorruptLogError``; a ``"torn"``
454	        terminal is left for the caller, which decides from the durable
455	        checkpoint whether it is a tail to discard or a gash to restore.
456	
457	        A compacted image starts with a base commit marker (``"b"``) that
458	        carries the pre-compaction sequence: it must be the first commit
459	        marker in the file, it establishes the expected sequence at
460	        ``seq + 1`` and no second base marker may ever follow. An ordinary
461	        first commit must still be sequence 1.
462	        """
463	        expected_seq = 1
464	        last_seq = 0
465	        committed_end = 0
466	        for meta, _value, _start, end in frames:
467	            op = meta.get("t")
468	            if op in (_OP_PUT, _OP_DELETE):
469	                key = meta.get("k")
470	                if not isinstance(key, str) or key == "":
471	                    raise CorruptLogError(
472	                        f"invalid frame metadata: {meta!r}")
473	            elif op == _OP_BASE:
474	                seq = meta.get("s")
475	                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
476	                    raise CorruptLogError(
477	                        f"invalid base commit marker: {meta!r}")
478	                if last_seq != 0:
479	                    raise CorruptLogError(
480	                        "base commit must be the first commit marker")
481	                if seq < 1:
482	                    raise CorruptLogError(
483	                        f"base commit sequence {seq} out of order")
484	                last_seq = seq
485	                expected_seq = seq + 1
486	                committed_end = end
487	            elif op == _OP_COMMIT:
488	                seq = meta.get("s")
489	                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
490	                    raise CorruptLogError(
491	                        f"invalid commit marker: {meta!r}")
492	                if seq != expected_seq:
493	                    raise CorruptLogError(
494	                        f"commit sequence {seq} out of order, "
495	                        f"expected {expected_seq}")
496	                last_seq = seq
497	                expected_seq += 1
498	                committed_end = end
499	            else:
500	                raise CorruptLogError(f"unknown frame type: {op!r}")
501	        if terminal is not None and terminal[0] == "invalid":
502	            raise CorruptLogError("corrupt log frame")
503	        return committed_end, last_seq
504	
505	    @staticmethod
506	    def _replay(frames) -> tuple[dict[str, bytes], int]:
507	        state: dict[str, bytes] = {}
508	        applied = 0
509	        for meta, value, _start, _end in frames:
510	            op = meta["t"]
511	            if op in _COMMIT_OPS:
512	                continue
513	            if op == _OP_PUT:
514	                state[meta["k"]] = value
515	            else:  # _OP_DELETE
516	                state.pop(meta["k"], None)
517	            applied += 1
518	        return state, applied
519	
520	    @staticmethod
521	    def _last_seq(frames) -> int:
522	        return max(
523	            (meta["s"] for meta, _v, _s, _e in frames
524	             if meta.get("t") in _COMMIT_OPS),
525	            default=0)
526	
527	    # -- crash-convergence sidecars ---------------------------------------
528	
529	    @staticmethod
530	    def _copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, length: int) -> None:
531	        remaining = length
532	        while remaining:
533	            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
534	            if not chunk:
535	                raise CorruptLogError(
536	                    "source ended before the committed prefix")
537	            fdst.write(chunk)
538	            remaining -= len(chunk)
539	        fdst.truncate(length)

541	    def _atomic_file(self, target: str, write) -> None:
542	        """Replace ``target`` atomically: temp file, fsync, rename, dir fsync."""
543	        tmp = target + ".tmp"
544	        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
545	            write(f)
546	            os.fsync(f.fileno())
547	        os.replace(tmp, target)
548	        _fsync_dir(self._dir)

550	    def _write_checkpoint(self, end: int) -> None:
551	        """Persist the log prefix ``[0, end)`` as the clean checkpoint."""
552	        if end <= 0:
553	            return
554	
555	        def write(fdst):
556	            with open(self._path, "rb") as fsrc:
557	                self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, end)
558	
559	        self._atomic_file(self._ckp_path, write)

561	    def _checkpoint_boundary(self) -> int:
562	        """Commit boundary the durable checkpoint covers; 0 if absent.
563	
564	        A checkpoint that is torn, unparseable or not exactly one committed
565	        prefix is corruption of the recovery machinery rather than a discard.
566	        """
567	        try:
568	            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._ckp_path)
569	        except FileNotFoundError:
570	            return 0
571	        if not frames:
572	            # An empty checkpoint covers the empty prefix; anything non-empty
573	            # that parses to no frames is corruption.
574	            if os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path) == 0 and terminal is None:
575	                return 0
576	            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint is not a clean committed prefix")
577	        if terminal is not None:
578	            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint is not a clean committed prefix")
579	        end, _seq = self._validate(frames, None)
580	        if end != os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path):
581	            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint has bytes past its commit")
582	        return end

584	    def _write_marker(self, clean_end: int, discarded: int) -> None:
585	        payload = json.dumps(
586	            {"end": clean_end, "discarded": discarded},
587	            separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
588	
589	        def write(f):
590	            f.write(payload)
591	
592	        self._atomic_file(self._marker_path, write)

594	    def _read_marker(self):
595	        try:
596	            with open(self._marker_path, "rb") as f:
597	                raw = f.read()
598	        except FileNotFoundError:
599	            return None
600	        try:
601	            marker = json.loads(raw)
602	            end = marker["end"]
603	            discarded = marker["discarded"]
604	        except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):
605	            raise CorruptLogError("unparseable recovery marker")
606	        if (not isinstance(end, int) or isinstance(end, bool) or end < 0
607	                or discarded not in (0, 1)):
608	            raise CorruptLogError("invalid recovery marker")
609	        return end, discarded

611	    def _remove_marker(self) -> None:
612	        try:
613	            os.unlink(self._marker_path)
614	        except FileNotFoundError:
615	            return
616	        _fsync_dir(self._dir)

618	    def _remove_stale_temps(self) -> None:
619	        for name in (self._path + ".tmp", self._ckp_path + ".tmp",
620	                     self._marker_path + ".tmp", self._cmp_path + ".tmp"):
621	            try:

626	    def _rebuild_log(self, clean_end: int) -> None:
627	        """Make the log exactly its clean ``[0, clean_end)`` prefix.
628	
629	        Kill-safe and idempotent: when a checkpoint covers the prefix the new
630	        log is fully written and fsynced as a temp file and atomically renamed
631	        over the old one, so a kill leaves either the old log or the complete
632	        restored log -- never a half-written file -- and rerunning converges.
633	        Without a checkpoint but with the committed bytes still at stable
634	        offsets, a synced truncate drops the tail instead. The empty prefix is
635	        a truncate to zero.
636	        """
637	        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
638	        if size == clean_end:
639	            return
640	
641	        if clean_end == 0:
642	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
643	            os.fsync(self._fd)
644	            return
645	
646	        try:
647	            ckp_size = os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path)
648	        except FileNotFoundError:
649	            ckp_size = -1
650	
651	        if ckp_size < clean_end and size > clean_end:
652	            # No checkpoint, but the committed bytes survive at stable
653	            # offsets: drop the dirty tail. Idempotent if killed mid-call.
654	            try:
655	                os.fsync(self._fd)
656	            except OSError:
657	                pass
658	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, clean_end)
659	            os.fsync(self._fd)
660	            return
661	        if ckp_size < clean_end:
662	            raise CorruptLogError(
663	                "committed prefix is torn and no checkpoint covers it")
664	
665	        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
666	        with open(self._ckp_path, "rb") as fsrc, open(tmp, "wb") as fdst:
667	            self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, clean_end)
668	            os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
669	        # Windows cannot rename over a path held open by the append fd.
670	        os.close(self._fd)
671	        try:
672	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
673	            _fsync_dir(self._dir)
674	        finally:
675	            self._fd = os.open(
676	                self._path,
677	                os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | _O_BINARY, 0o644)

683	    def _build_compact_image(self, seq: int) -> tuple[bytes, int]:
684	        """Serialise the committed state into one compact log image.
685	
686	        One put frame per live key, keys in sorted order, followed by a base
687	        commit marker carrying the pre-compaction sequence. The empty state
688	        at seq 0 is an empty image rather than a zero-sequence marker.
689	        """
690	        if seq == 0:
691	            return b"", 0
692	        parts = [_encode_frame(_OP_PUT, value, key=key)
693	                 for key, value in sorted(self._data.items())]
694	        parts.append(_encode_frame(_OP_BASE, seq=seq))
695	        return b"".join(parts), len(self._data)

697	    def _read_compact_candidate(self):
698	        """Validate ``wal.cmp`` as one compacted image.
699	
700	        Returns ``(image, end, seq, live)`` where ``image`` is the exact
701	        byte content, or ``None`` when the sidecar is absent. The image must
702	        be a clean file ending exactly on a base commit marker, preceded only
703	        by put frames with strictly increasing keys; anything else is
704	        corruption of the crash-convergence machinery, never a discardable
705	        tail (the sidecar is always atomically replaced, never written in
706	        place).
707	        """
708	        try:
709	            f = open(self._cmp_path, "rb")
710	        except FileNotFoundError:
711	            return None
712	        with f:
713	            image = f.read()
714	        if not image:
715	            # An empty candidate encodes the empty state at seq 0.
716	            return b"", 0, 0, 0
717	
718	        frames, terminal = self._scan_bytes(image)
719	        if terminal is not None:
720	            raise CorruptLogError(
721	                "compaction candidate is not a clean committed prefix")
722	        end, seq = self._validate(frames, None)
723	        if end != len(image) or seq <= 0:
724	            raise CorruptLogError(
725	                "compaction candidate has bytes past its base commit")
726	        live = 0
727	        last_key: str | None = None
728	        saw_base = False
729	        for meta, _value, _start, _end in frames:
730	            op = meta.get("t")
731	            if op == _OP_PUT:
732	                if saw_base:
733	                    raise CorruptLogError(
734	                        "compaction candidate has puts past its base commit")
735	                key = meta["k"]
736	                if last_key is not None and key <= last_key:
737	                    raise CorruptLogError(
738	                        "compaction candidate keys are not sorted uniquely")
739	                last_key = key
740	                live += 1
741	            elif op == _OP_BASE:
742	                if saw_base:
743	                    raise CorruptLogError(
744	                        "compaction candidate has multiple base commits")
745	                saw_base = True
746	            else:
747	                raise CorruptLogError(
748	                    "compaction candidate contains a non-compacted frame")
749	        if not saw_base:
750	            raise CorruptLogError(
751	                "compaction candidate ends without a base commit")

754	    def _scan_bytes(self, data: bytes):
755	        """Frame-scan raw bytes as if they were a log file."""
756	        frames = []
757	        terminal = None
758	        with io.BytesIO(data) as f:
759	            for event in _iter_frames(f):
760	                if event[0] == "frame":
761	                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
762	                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
763	                else:
764	                    terminal = event
765	        return frames, terminal

767	    def _install_log_bytes(self, image: bytes) -> None:
768	        """Atomically replace the log with ``image`` and reopen the fd.
769	
770	        The complete image is written and fsynced as a temp file first, so a
771	        kill leaves either the old log or the complete new one -- never a
772	        half-written log. The append fd is closed for the rename because
773	        Windows cannot replace a path held open by it, then reopened.
774	        """
775	        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
776	        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
777	            f.write(image)
778	            f.truncate(len(image))
779	            os.fsync(f.fileno())
780	        os.close(self._fd)
781	        try:
782	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
783	            _fsync_dir(self._dir)
784	        finally:
785	            self._fd = os.open(
786	                self._path,
787	                os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | _O_BINARY, 0o644)

791	    def _install_compaction(self, image: bytes, seq: int) -> None:
792	        """Publish a staged compacted image; idempotent and kill-safe.
793	
794	        The torn-tail marker is dropped first: its byte offset belongs to
795	        the old (longer) log and must not outlive the shrink. Checkpoint is
796	        replaced next and the log last, both via complete-file atomic
797	        renames, then the candidate is removed. Any ordering of a kill
798	        between those steps leaves the durable files equal to either the old
799	        pair or the complete new pair, and rerunning (via the surviving
800	        candidate) converges to the same compacted bytes.
801	        """
802	        # Compaction closes any prior recovery epoch the way a commit does;
803	        # do it while the old log still exists so a later kill replays this
804	        # whole publish from the durable candidate.
805	        self._remove_marker()
806	
807	        if seq == 0:
808	            # Empty committed state: the log is zero length and there is no
809	            # checkpoint to publish; reclaim every old byte and drop the plan.
810	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
811	            os.fsync(self._fd)
812	            try:
813	                os.unlink(self._ckp_path)
814	                _fsync_dir(self._dir)
815	            except FileNotFoundError:
816	                pass
817	            self._remove_candidate()
818	            return
819	
820	        def write(fdst):
821	            fdst.write(image)
822	
823	        self._atomic_file(self._ckp_path, write)
824	        self._install_log_bytes(image)
825	        self._remove_candidate()

827	    def _remove_candidate(self) -> None:
828	        try:
829	            os.unlink(self._cmp_path)
830	        except FileNotFoundError:
831	            return
832	        _fsync_dir(self._dir)

834	    def _finish_compaction(self) -> None:
835	        """Complete a compaction interrupted after its candidate went durable.
836	
837	        With a single writer a present candidate means its compaction never
838	        finished (no later commit was possible), so the log and checkpoint
839	        cannot be ahead of it; the publish is simply repeated. A candidate
840	        whose boundary a newer durable epoch has overtaken is stale and is
841	        discarded instead.
842	        """
843	        candidate = self._read_compact_candidate()
844	        if candidate is None:
845	            return
846	        image, _end, cand_seq, _live = candidate
847	
848	        log_seq = 0
849	        if os.path.exists(self._path):
850	            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._path)
851	            _log_end, log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
852	        ckp_seq = 0
853	        ckp = self._read_clean_prefix(self._ckp_path)
854	        if ckp is not None:
855	            _frames, _end, ckp_seq = ckp
856	        if max(log_seq, ckp_seq) > cand_seq:
857	            # A newer committed epoch exists; the staged image is obsolete.
858	            self._remove_candidate()

862	    def _converge(self):
863	        """Validate and converge the on-disk log to its clean state.
864	
865	        Returns ``(frames, discarded)`` for the now-clean log. Raises
866	        ``CorruptLogError`` without changing anything if the log is corrupt.
867	        Safe to run repeatedly and safe to kill at any point.
868	
869	        The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log
870	        boundary, the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can
871	        never regress. A log torn inside its committed prefix is rebuilt from
872	        the checkpoint and ``discarded`` stays 0 (those bytes were committed,
873	        not an unfinished write); a torn or merely uncommitted tail past the
874	        boundary is discarded, and the marker freezes that report until the
875	        next commit even when the kill lands mid-repair.
876	        """
877	        self._remove_stale_temps()
878	        # A durable compaction candidate left by a killed compact() is
879	        # published before ordinary convergence; it is itself a complete
880	        # committed prefix, so this never invents or loses a committed byte.
881	        self._finish_compaction()
882	        marker = self._read_marker()
883	        marker_end = -1
884	        marker_discarded = 0
885	        if marker is not None:
886	            marker_end, marker_discarded = marker
887	
888	        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
889	        log_end, _log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
890	        ckp_end = self._checkpoint_boundary()
891	        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
892	
893	        target = max(log_end, ckp_end, marker_end)
894	        # The target bytes must come from somewhere still on disk: the
895	        # validated log itself or the checkpoint.
896	        if target > log_end and target > ckp_end:
897	            raise CorruptLogError("recovery target has no durable source")
898	
899	        log_clean = terminal is None and size == log_end
900	
901	        if log_clean and log_end == target:
902	            # Nothing to repair. An old marker whose epoch a newer commit
903	            # closed durably can finally go; otherwise its discarded count
904	            # stays frozen until that commit.
905	            if marker is not None:
906	                if target > marker_end:
907	                    self._remove_marker()
908	                    discarded = 0
909	                else:
910	                    discarded = marker_discarded
911	            else:
912	                discarded = 0
913	            if ckp_end < target:
914	                self._write_checkpoint(target)
915	            return frames, discarded
916	
917	        if target > log_end:
918	            # Committed bytes were torn away (offset 0 included): the
919	            # checkpoint is the source of truth. The discarded count is only
920	            # meaningful when the marker pins this exact boundary.
921	            discarded = marker_discarded if target == marker_end else 0
922	            self._rebuild_log(target)
923	        else:
924	            # A dirty suffix sits past the boundary. Decide discarded from
925	            # the suffix itself: a torn final record counts, complete
926	            # uncommitted frames do not. This also covers a repair killed
927	            # before the rebuild (the original suffix is still here, so the
928	            # same decision is reached) and fresh writes appended after a
929	            # previous repair (a new crash is a new decision rather than the
930	            # old marker's). A marker is only frozen once the log itself is
931	            # rebuilt clean; see the clean branch above.
932	            discarded = 1 if terminal is not None else 0
933	            if ckp_end < target:
934	                # Make the prefix independently restorable before we publish
935	                # the plan or remove any bytes.
936	                self._write_checkpoint(target)
937	            self._write_marker(target, discarded)
938	            self._rebuild_log(target)
939	
940	        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
941	        end, _seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
942	        if end != target or terminal is not None:
943	            raise CorruptLogError("restore did not converge")
944	        return frames, discarded

950	        self._entries = len(frames)

952	        self._touched = {}
953	        self._discarded = discarded

967	    def _open_read_only(self) -> None:
968	        """Pin a committed snapshot without creating or modifying anything.
969	
970	        No lock is taken and nothing on disk is written. The reader chooses
971	        the highest committed prefix available at the instant it opens --
972	        the validated prefix of ``wal.log`` or the existing ``wal.ckp``
973	        sidecar, which the writer replaces atomically as part of every
974	        commit -- scans that prefix once into memory, and serves every
975	        ``get`` from that index. Later reads are independent of log history,
976	        never replay the log and never block the writer.
977	
978	        The checkpoint is a complete, self-contained image that is never
979	        modified in place (only atomically replaced), so reading it cannot
980	        expose uncommitted bytes, a half-written commit, a torn record or a
981	        half-finished rebuild/shrink. It is also what makes the pin safe once
982	        the reader closes the file: the image survives any later rename.
983	        """
984	        frames, end, seq = self._choose_readonly_prefix()
985	        state, _applied = self._replay(frames)

991	    def _choose_readonly_prefix(self):
992	        """Return ``(frames, end, seq)`` for the highest committed snapshot.
993	
994	        Takes the higher of the validated log boundary and the checkpoint
995	        boundary, mirroring the writer's durable-boundary rule. A torn or
996	        merely uncommitted tail past the last commit is excluded; a framing
997	        or sequence failure in committed bytes is corruption and raises
998	        ``CorruptLogError``. The checkpoint is the source when a crash or a
999	        concurrent rebuild has torn/shrunk the committed log bytes.
1000	        """
1001	        log_frames = None
1002	        log_end = -1
1003	        log_seq = 0
1004	        if os.path.exists(self._path):
1005	            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._path)
1006	            log_end, log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
1007	            # Keep only frames at or before the last commit; the torn final
1008	            # record already arrives as the terminal, not as a frame.
1009	            log_frames = [fr for fr in frames if fr[3] <= log_end]
1010	
1011	        ckp = self._read_clean_prefix(self._ckp_path)
1012	        if ckp is None:
1013	            if log_frames is None:
1014	                return [], 0, 0
1015	            return log_frames, log_end, log_seq
1016	
1017	        ckp_frames, ckp_end, ckp_seq = ckp
1018	        if log_end >= ckp_end:
1019	            return log_frames, log_end, log_seq

1022	    def _read_clean_prefix(self, path: str):
1023	        """Validate ``path`` as an exact committed prefix.

1025	        Returns ``(frames, end, seq)`` or ``None`` if the file is absent.
1026	        Raises ``CorruptLogError`` when it exists but is not exactly a clean
1027	        committed prefix: such a sidecar is replaced atomically, so a torn
1028	        or unparseable image cannot be a publish caught mid-flight. The size
1029	        used for the "bytes past its commit" check is taken from the same
1030	        open inode that was scanned, so a concurrent atomic replace can
1031	        never mix the bytes of one version with the size of another.
1032	        """
1033	        try:
1034	            f = open(path, "rb")
1035	        except FileNotFoundError:
1036	            return None
1037	        with f:
1038	            frames = []
1039	            terminal = None
1040	            for event in _iter_frames(f):
1041	                if event[0] == "frame":
1042	                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
1043	                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
1044	                else:
1045	                    terminal = event

1047	        if terminal is not None:
1048	            raise CorruptLogError("sidecar is not a clean committed prefix")

1062	    def _committed_view(self) -> dict[str, bytes]:
1063	        """The writer's committed state, undoing uncommitted session edits.
1064	
1065	        ``self._data`` folds uncommitted puts/deletes into the committed
1066	        state; ``self._touched`` remembers what each touched key held at the
1067	        last commit (``None`` when absent), so the committed snapshot is
1068	        recovered without replaying the log. With nothing pending the live
1069	        dict is returned as is -- the caller copies it into the cursor.
1070	        """

1072	            return self._data

1074	        for key, old in self._touched.items():

1123	    def scan(self, start: str | None = None,
1124	             end: str | None = None) -> ScanCursor:
1125	        """Open an ordered cursor over the pinned committed snapshot.
1126	
1127	        The cursor yields ``(key, value)`` pairs in bytewise key order --
1128	        keys compared by their raw UTF-8 bytes, values returned as the exact
1129	        stored bytes -- covering ``start`` (inclusive) through ``end``
1130	        (exclusive). A ``None`` endpoint leaves that side unbounded, so
1131	        ``scan()`` walks the whole snapshot. Keys that only ever appeared in
1132	        delete records are absent, a key overwritten any number of times
1133	        yields only its last committed value, and empty values scan like any
1134	        other. A writer's uncommitted session changes are not part of the
1135	        snapshot; a read-only store scans the snapshot it pinned at open.
1136

1138	        independent of later commits, compaction, crash recovery and log
1139	        space reclamation, and its cost is independent of the log's history
1140	        length. A ``start`` that sorts after ``end`` raises ``ValueError``,
1141	        as does reading from the cursor after it is closed.

1143	        self._ensure_open()

1145	            if endpoint is not None and not isinstance(endpoint, str):
1146	                raise TypeError("scan endpoints must be strings or None")

1148	        hi = end.encode("utf-8") if end is not None else None
1149	        if lo is not None and hi is not None and lo > hi:

1151	                f"scan start {start!r} sorts after scan end {end!r}")

1154	        items = []
1155	        for key, value in data.items():
1156	            key_bytes = key.encode("utf-8")
1157	            if lo is not None and key_bytes < lo:
1158	                continue
1159	            if hi is not None and key_bytes >= hi:
1160	                continue
1161	            items.append((key_bytes, key, bytes(value)))
1162	        items.sort(key=lambda item: item[0])

1201	        ``discarded`` is 1 when a single torn final record was dropped (0
1202	        otherwise) and ``seq`` is the durable sequence number after recovery.
1203	        Raises ``CorruptLogError`` (a ``ValueError``) if the log is corrupt;
1204	        nothing is applied or truncated in that case.

1207	        times and rerunning converges to the same state and the same report
1208	        as one clean recovery, and the next commit always uses ``seq + 1``.

1232	    def compact(self) -> dict:
1233	        """Rewrite committed history into one tight, kill-safe log image.
1234	
1235	        The log becomes exactly the currently committed state: one put frame
1236	        per live key (sorted by key) followed by a base commit marker that
1237	        carries the pre-compaction sequence number. Deleted keys are gone for
1238	        good, the durable sequence keeps its value (the next commit is
